articles.title: Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials

abstract.text: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.

articles.title: Systemic Hypertension and Survival in Pulmonary Hypertension

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a progressive and life-threatening condition with rising prevalence among older adults, frequently coexists with systemic hypertension, the prognostic impact of which is poorly understood.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the association between systemic hypertension and survival in patients with PH.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This multicenter cohort study analyzed data from the Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute GoDeep meta-registry, integrating global retrospective and prospective PH cohorts (n = 3238 in Europe, n = 3014 in North America, n = 96 in Africa, n = 802 in Asia, and n = 851 in Oceania). Survival was assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and adjusted for key confounders, with sensitivity analyses to validate robustness. Independent external validation was performed in a cohort in the UK. A total of 12 771 patients with incident PH (median [IQR] age, 65 [53-73] years; 7372 [58%] female) were diagnosed via right heart catheterization and comprehensive clinical data, encompassing PH groups 1-5 and all age categories. The study spans diagnosis decades from 1980 to 2020. Data were analyzed from February 2025 until September 2026.

abstract.label: EXPOSURES
abstract.text: Center-reported diagnosis of systemic hypertension, baseline systolic systemic arterial pressure (sSAP), and heart rate as well as longitudinal sSAP and heart rate trajectories.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: All-cause mortality, adjusted for confounding variables, including age, PH group, antihypertensive and PH-specific medications, and cardiac index.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Higher baseline sSAP and preexisting systemic hypertension were independently associated with improved survival. Patients with hypertension exhibited a 26% reduced mortality hazard (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74; 95% CI, 0.68-0.79) compared to their counterparts without hypertension. Survival benefits correlated positively with increasing sSAP (80-180 mm Hg), remained consistent across PH groups and age groups, and were independent of antihypertensive and PH-specific medications. Elevated heart rate was associated with higher mortality. sSAP increments correlated with improved cardiac index and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion. Decreased sSAP and higher heart rate during follow-up correlated with higher mortality. External validation in a separate UK cohort confirmed these findings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this global PH cohort, higher sSAP was associated with enhanced survival, while a higher baseline heart rate and declining systemic blood pressure during follow-up were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

articles.conclusion: In this global PH cohort, higher sSAP was associated with enhanced survival, while a higher baseline heart rate and declining systemic blood pressure during follow-up were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

articles.title: Periprocedural Pulmonary Hypertension and Outcomes After Mitral Valve Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes remains uncertain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study sought to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as having no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH, or residual PH according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of residual and new-onset PH.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: No PH was observed in 1,432 patients (41.1%), normalized PH in 763 (21.9%), new-onset PH in 298 (8.6%), and residual PH in 991 (28.4%). The 2-year incidence of the primary endpoint differed significantly across groups (17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6%, respectively; P < 0.001). Normalized PH showed outcomes comparable to no PH (adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.78-1.24). In contrast, new-onset PH (HR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.10-1.93) and residual PH (HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.13-1.68) were independently associated with adverse outcomes. Severe tricuspid regurgitation, baseline TRPG >50 mm Hg, and tricuspid annular dilation predicted residual PH, whereas residual mitral regurgitation and postprocedural transmitral gradients >5 mm Hg predicted new-onset PH.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment and Prognosis of Heart Valve Registry; UMIN-ID: UMIN000023653.

articles.conclusion: Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment and Prognosis of Heart Valve Registry; UMIN-ID: UMIN000023653.

articles.title: HFSA Scientific Statement on Right Heart Failure

abstract.text: Right heart failure (RHF), both acute and chronic is increasingly recognized as a distinct and clinically significant syndrome across the spectrum of cardiovascular disease. Estimates suggest RHF complicates >25-30% of hospitalizations for acute decompensated HF and is nearly universal in advanced pulmonary hypertension (PH) (1) Despite recent diagnostic and therapeutic advancements, RHF remains associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and impaired quality of life. Addressing RHF requires dedicated strategies tailored to its pathophysiology, including early identification, risk stratification, and novel therapies. (2) While randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on the topic remain limited, there has been increasing emphasis on early recognition and management of RHF (especially in the setting of left ventricular [LV] failure). In addition, there is an expanding role for temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in acute RHF and percutaneous tricuspid interventions in chronic RHF. Yet, the field remains limited by its under-recognition, lack of standardized definitions, and limited therapeutic options, which underscore the urgent need for consensus and guidance.

articles.title: Exercise Right Atrial Stiffness From Pressure-Volume Loops and Prognosis in Pulmonary Hypertension

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In pulmonary hypertension (PH), risk assessment focuses on right ventricular function and may overlook exercise-related right atrial (RA) functional limitation. We investigated whether RA stiffness during exercise reflects impaired right-heart filling reserve and is associated with prognosis beyond conventional measures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We prospectively enrolled 68 participants in this observational study, including 42 with precapillary PH. Participants who had PH ruled out and patients with postcapillary PH formed reference groups. Participants underwent 3-dimensional echocardiography, right heart catheterization, and invasive RA pressure-volume loop analysis at rest and during standardized semisupine exercise. RA filling stiffness was derived from the reservoir phase. Patients with precapillary PH were stratified by median exercise RA filling stiffness.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At rest, high- and low-stiffness groups had comparable right ventricular function, afterload, and cardiac index, but the high-stiffness group exhibited impaired phasic RA strain and venous congestion (median [interquartile range] liver stiffness, 7.1 [6.0-8.8] versus 5.2 [4.8-5.8] kPa; P=0.021). During exercise, mean RA pressure increased similarly, but the high-stiffness group had impaired peak cardiac index (3.3±1.0 versus 4.1±0.9 L/min per m2; P=0.015) and RA strain. Unlike resting RA stiffness, high exercise RA stiffness was independently associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 4.37 [95% CI, 1.20-15.96]). A model including RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve discriminated high RA stiffness (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.90).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: RA stiffness during exercise integrates resting congestion with limited cardiac reserve and unmasks mortality risk missed by resting metrics. RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve noninvasively identify the high-stiffness subgroup.

articles.conclusion: RA stiffness during exercise integrates resting congestion with limited cardiac reserve and unmasks mortality risk missed by resting metrics. RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve noninvasively identify the high-stiffness subgroup.

articles.title: Shock With Acute Myocardial Dysfunction in Stercoral Colitis: Diagnosis and Management

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Shock in sepsis is predominantly vasodilatory; however, concomitant myocardial dysfunction may result in superimposed cardiogenic shock and a mixed shock state.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 75-year-old man with Parkinson disease, severe constipation, and stercoral colitis presented with profound shock after an enema. Echocardiography showed new biventricular dysfunction with regional wall-motion abnormalities. Invasive hemodynamic assessment demonstrated elevated filling pressures, low cardiac index, and low systemic vascular resistance despite substantial vasoactive and inotropic support, consistent with a mixed vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock. He improved after antibiotics and vasoactive support, but manual disimpaction after stabilization was followed within minutes by recurrent/similar shock.

abstract.label: REVIEW SUMMARY
abstract.text: This case illustrates a practical approach to mixed shock with acute myocardial dysfunction. Treatment of underlying infection should occur in parallel with characterization of the hemodynamic phenotype. Serial echocardiography and invasive hemodynamic assessment can identify concomitant vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support as shock physiology evolves.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Shock physiology is dynamic. In patients with sepsis, serial clinical, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic reassessment can identify concomitant cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support.

articles.title: Not All PVR Reductions Are Created Equal: Lessons From the CADENCE Trial
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstract.text: The CADENCE trial evaluated sotatercept in combined post- and pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (CpcPH-HFpEF). We analyzed the pathophysiological implications of the observed pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) reduction.A hemodynamic comparison was conducted contrasting the mechanistic effects of sotaercept with conventional pulmonary vasodilators.In CADENCE, PVR and pressure reductions occurred without marked cardiac output augmentation, contrasting with flow-mediated recruitment typical of traditional vasodilators. Sotatercept-induced PVR reduction may reflect true vascular reverse remodeling rather than vasodilation, underscoring the need to discriminate resistance reduction mechanisms in CpcPHHFpEF.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Indices of Right Ventricular Function are Associated with Adverse Clinical Outcomes Across Heart Failure Subtypes

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: While right ventricular dysfunction (RVD) is critical to the progression of heart failure (HF), the prevalence and prognostic implications of RVD across HF subtypes remains poorly understood.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We aimed to characterize differences in hemodynamic indices of RVD among patients with HF with preserved (HFpEF, EF≥50%) vs reduced (HFrEF, EF<50%) ejection fraction and examine associations of RVD with longitudinal clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We identified patients with prevalent HF undergoing clinically indicated right heart catheterization at Massachusetts General Hospital (2005-2016). We examined three RV hemodynamic indices: right atrial to wedge pressure ratio (RA/PCWP), RV stroke work index (RVSWI), and pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi). We used multivariable Cox models to examine the association of each index with HF hospitalizations (HFH) and death.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 2,062 patients, 1,242 (60%) had HFrEF and 820 (40%) had HFpEF; 56% of individuals with HFrEF and 53% with HFpEF met at least one hemodynamic criterion for RVD. In HFrEF, lower PAPi was associated with greater risk of HFH (HR 0.84 [0.77, 0.92]), and higher RVSWI was associated with greater risk of death (HR 1.17, [1.07, 1.27], all p<0.001). By contrast, only higher RA/PCWP was associated with greater risk of death in HFpEF (HR 1.11 (1.00, 1.22); p=0.046).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hemodynamic RVD is common in both HFrEF and HFpEF, and hemodynamic measures of RV function are associated with greater risk of adverse outcomes. Importantly, the prognostic value of RV indices varied by HF subtype, highlighting key differences in the role of RVD in HFrEF vs HFpEF.

articles.conclusion: Hemodynamic RVD is common in both HFrEF and HFpEF, and hemodynamic measures of RV function are associated with greater risk of adverse outcomes. Importantly, the prognostic value of RV indices varied by HF subtype, highlighting key differences in the role of RVD in HFrEF vs HFpEF.

articles.title: Right Atrial Phasic Function Improves CMR-Based Prognostication in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Study

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: In multiple cardiovascular diseases, right atrial (RA) function can serve as an independent predictor for the clinical status and prognosis. However, the prognostic value of RA strain in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) remains considerably unknown. This study aims to explore the relationships between RA strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging-feature tracking (CMR-FT) and adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: This retrospective study enrolled patients with HFmrEF who were referred for echocardiography and CMR at two tertiary medical centers from April 2016 to September 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF-related hospitalization and cardiac transplantation. The findings were validated in a cohort of patients with HFmrEF enrolled from two additional tertiary care centers (January 2019 to January 2025). The development cohort included 1317 patients, and the validation cohort comprised 385 patients. During a median follow-up period of 2.8 years and 2.1 years, respectively, 243 and 72 patients in the development cohort and validation cohort reached the primary endpoint, respectively. Cox regression analysis showed that RA conduit strain was an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR: 0.86 [0.82, 0.90]; P < .001). The full model integrating clinical variables, traditional imaging, and RA strain achieved the best predictive performance (C-index: 0.80 in development, 0.81 in validation cohorts).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​.

articles.conclusion: RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​.

articles.title: Novel cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging biomarkers to track response to treatment including Sotatercept in a patient with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension: a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes progressive right ventricular (RV) pressure overload and left ventricular (LV) underfilling. Sotatercept is an activin-signal inhibitor, approved by FDA in 2024 and EMA in 2025, as an add-on treatment in adult patients with PAH. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived atrioventricular plane displacement (AVPD) and left ventricular pressure-volume (PV) loops may represent non-invasive markers of treatment response, particularly important as novel therapies addressing remodelling emerge.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 30-year-old woman was diagnosed with idiopathic PAH, after presenting with dyspnoea and peripheral oedema. Baseline CMR showed severe RV dilation, reduced RV ejection fraction, and low indexed LV stroke volume, with reduced bilateral AVPD and markedly impaired LV PV loop indices, with low stroke work, low mean external power, and high ventriculo-arterial coupling. Initial dual PAH therapy, with an endothelin receptor antagonist and a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor initially improved symptoms, pulmonary vascular resistance, as well as AVPD and PV loop derived indices, whereas conventional CMR indices showed only minimal change. One year later, despite triple therapy, including prostacyclin analogue, the patient deteriorated clinically and CMR showed worsening of AVPD and PV loop indices. Treatment escalation with Sotatercept immediately improved clinical status, haemodynamic, AVPD, and PV loop indices despite persistent RV remodelling.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Serial CMR-derived AVPD and LV PV loops may provide clinically useful additional information during longitudinal follow-up of PAH patients, especially in those approaching maximal available medical therapies. In the present case, both AVPD and LV PV loops reflected treatment response, and showed significant improvement after initiation of Sotatercept.

articles.title: CCR2-Dependent Myeloid Cell Recruitment Links Post-MI Heart Failure to Pulmonary Hypertension

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease (PH-LHD) is a common complication of myocardial infarction (MI) and heart failure (HF). Myeloid inflammation is a major hallmark of both the local cardiac and systemic post-MI response, with resident and recruited monocyte-derived macrophages orchestrating each step of the ensuing inflammatory cascade, from clearance of dead cardiomyocytes to scar tissue formation. Similarly, myeloid inflammation is a key feature of the PH lung, driving remodeling of small pulmonary vessels. We thus hypothesized that MI-induced systemic myeloid inflammation contributes directly to the development of PH-LHD.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We assessed expression of inflammatory adhesion molecules, as markers of vascular inflammatory activation and myeloid cell recruitment pathways, in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, PH-LHD, as well as in a PH-LHD rat model. We then induced MI and subsequent HF in 8- to 10-week-old female C57BL/6J mice via permanent ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. HF mice were then treated with a CCR2 (C-C chemokine receptor 2) antagonist to block monocyte recruitment and the development of PH-LHD was assessed at 6 weeks post-MI by a combination of invasive hemodynamics, flow cytometry, echocardiography, and lung histology.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Expression of key inflammatory adhesion molecules, including VCAM1 and SELE, was increased in PH-LHD lungs from humans and rats. Following early post-MI development of HF with reduced ejection fraction, mice exhibited increased numbers of circulating monocytes, lung monocytes, and lung interstitial macrophages, as well as PH-LHD by 6 weeks, characterized by right ventricular hypertrophy, elevated right ventricular pressures, and lung vascular remodeling of small-to-medium-sized pulmonary vessels. Administration of the selective CCR2 antagonist RS102895 from day 10 post-MI to reduce monocyte tissue recruitment attenuated lung vascular remodeling, right ventricular systolic and diastolic pressures, right ventricular hypertrophy, and lung adhesion molecule expression at 6 weeks, compared with vehicle-treated controls, without improving the underlying left-sided HF.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates a causal role for CCR2-dependent myeloid cell recruitment in the progression from MI-induced HF to secondary pulmonary vascular disease.

articles.conclusion: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates a causal role for CCR2-dependent myeloid cell recruitment in the progression from MI-induced HF to secondary pulmonary vascular disease.

articles.title: Ovarian Hormone Decline Aggravates Cardiometabolic Risk and Accelerates Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction in Female ZSF1 Rats
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.journal_abbrev: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.ta: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstract.text: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is more prevalent in women than men at higher ages, suggesting an impact of ovarian hormone decrease on disease development. However, the basis of this relationship is incompletely understood. Obese female ZSF1 rats, an established cardiometabolic HFpEF model, were ovariectomized at 5-6 weeks of age (Ov-ZSF1, n=11) or stayed intact (O-ZSF1, n=11). The manifestation of HFpEF was analyzed and compared to lean control rats (L-ZSF1, n=11) using echocardiography, invasive hemodynamics, vascular function and histology. At 20 weeks of age O-ZSF1 rats were obese and had metabolic syndrome and HFpEF. These characteristics were further pronounced in Ov-ZSF1: body weight +36%, heart weight +13%, systolic blood pressure +29%, peripheral blood glucose +19%, NT-proBNP +35%, left ventricular (LV)-end-diastolic pressure +26% and E/e' ratio +10%. The rise of E/e' ratio, a key HFpEF feature, was seen earliest in Ov-ZSF1, indicating accelerated diastolic dysfunction. Systolic function was generally unchanged but the diastolic function was increasingly affected according to L-ZSF1<O-ZSF1<Ov-ZSF1. No histological evidence for pro-fibrotic remodeling was found but the obese groups showed >10% increased cardiomyocyte diameter in septum and more macrophage infiltration into the heart, representing cardiac remodeling processes. Compared to L-ZSF1 the maximum contractibility of right carotid vessel specimen was increased in O-ZSF1 (+5%) and Ov-ZSF1 (+7%). Disturbed dilatation capacity (-29%) was observed in Ov-ZSF1 only. Concluding, a decrease of ovarian hormone accelerates cardiometabolic HFpEF progression in female ZSF1 rats through combined metabolic, hemodynamic, cardiac, and vascular abnormalities, without overt myocardial fibrosis in female ZSF1rats.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Afterload Across the Pulmonary Hypertension Spectrum
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.journal_abbrev: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.ta: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstract.text: Right ventricular (RV) performance is the major determinant in pulmonary hypertension (PH). RV afterload is typically assessed using pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) and pulmonary arterial (PA) compliance, overlooking the dynamic component of pulsatile load. Characteristic impedance serves as a measurement of the opposition to pulsatile flow in the proximal arteries. Combined post- and precapillary PH (CpcPH) represents a growing and therapeutically challenging subgroup whose hemodynamic profile remains incompletely characterized. Our aim was to comprehensively describe RV afterload components across the PH spectrum and to evaluate their associations with RV morphology and function. We applied the time-domain method reported in literature to calculate characteristic impedance in a prospective cohort of 78 patients with PH undergoing right heart catheterization and cardiac magnetic resonance. PVR, PA compliance, and characteristic impedance were assessed and compared across precapillary PH (PAH and CTEPH), isolated post-capillary PH (IpcPH), or CpcPH. IpcPH exhibited higher compliance (2.3 mL/mmHg [1.9-3.4]) and lower impedance and PVR (84.5 [63.8-112.2] and 186.0 dyn.s.cm-5 [139.4-208.0] respectively). CpcPH showed intermediate values (1.8 mL/mmHg [1.0-2.7]; 120.4 [88.3-177.7] and 384.8 dyn.s.cm-5 [257.5-627.9]) between IpcPH and precapillary PH (1.4 mL/mmHg [1.1-2.1], 182.5 [123.4-231.4] and 524.1 [367.9-714.5] dyn.s.cm-5), with values closer to the precapillary end of the spectrum. We concluded that CpcPH occupies an intermediate hemodynamic phenotype within the PH spectrum, with some patients showing substantial overlap in afterload components with PAH and CTEPH patients. We observed that characteristic impedance provided complementary information on RV afterload beyond conventional metrics, supporting its integration into multimodal hemodynamic assessment.

articles.title: Resolution of Lancisi's sign following bicaval TricValve implantation for torrential tricuspid regurgitation: a case report defining a novel bedside marker of haemodynamic recovery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Caval valve implantation (CAVI) using the TricValve system is an emerging treatment option for severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) in patients who are unsuitable for surgery or orthotopic transcatheter intervention. Lancisi's sign is a classical manifestation of severe TR; however, its resolution after CAVI has not been described.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: An 85-year-old woman with recurrent right heart failure and torrential TR presented with prominent bilateral Lancisi's sign. Echocardiography revealed severe annular dilatation (48 mm), right ventricular dysfunction (TAPSE, 13 mm), and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40%. Owing to prohibitive surgical risk (EuroSCORE II 18.4%; TRI SCORE 14), she underwent successful implantation of 29-mm superior vena cava and 35-mm inferior vena cava TricValve prostheses. At 3 months, Lancisi's sign had completely resolved, NYHA functional class improved from III-IV to I-II, NT-proBNP decreased from 25 000 to 2 000 pg/mL, TAPSE increased from 13 to 20 mm, and no rehospitalization or device-related adverse event occurred. We report a structured single-patient case using clinical examination, echocardiography, invasive hemodynamic assessment, laboratory markers, and 3-month follow-up after bicaval TricValve implantation.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Bicaval TricValve implantation resulted in marked symptomatic, biochemical, echocardiographic, and bedside clinical improvements. The resolution of Lancisi's sign may represent a simple marker of hemodynamic recovery after CAVI.

articles.title: Role of digital health in the personalized management of heart failure due to Fontan failure: a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Heart failure (HF) represents a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with Fontan circulation. Chronic venous congestion, impaired preload, and limited cardiac output reserve make clinical assessment and intermittent invasive evaluations insufficient to capture early haemodynamic deterioration. Pharmacological treatment lack of robust evidence in this subgroup of patients. In this challenging setting, implantable invasive haemodynamic monitoring systems may provide continuous, real-life information capable of guiding personalized HF management.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 26-year-old Fontan male developed protein losing enteropathy and recurrent hospitalizations for decompensated heart failure. Therefore, the patient was candidate to heart transplantation. Over time, episodes of acute HF increased with an escalating requirement of dosage of diuretics. At 22 years of age, another episode of acute decompensated HF prompted a catheter-based intervention with Fontan conduit re-dilatation and re-fenestration with an Atrial Flow Regulator (AFR) implant, and a pulmonary artery pressure monitoring system (CardioMEMS™) was deployed to telemonitor pulmonary artery pressures and adjust the diuretic therapy accordingly. Up to date, 4 years from the intervention, the use of this remote monitoring system was feasible and effective in tailoring medical therapy to prevent further hospitalizations for acute HF. The patient is in clinical follow-up with regular controls.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Systems allowing continuous or repeated assessment of haemodynamic status in real-life conditions may support personalized treatment adjustments, improve symptom control, and potentially reduce HF-related hospitalizations in patients with failing Fontan circulation.
