articles.title: Genotype, Phenotypic Severity, and Survival in Pediatric Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Report From the Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Registry

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) frequently presents with heart failure in children. Whether a genetic cause of DCM is associated with disease severity or eventual outcome in pediatric DCM is unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A multiinstitutional prospective pediatric cohort study (0-18 years) with nonsyndromic DCM was undertaken from 2013 to 2016. A panel of 37 cardiomyopathy-associated genes was interrogated by exome sequencing with analysis for pathogenic or likely pathogenic (LP) variants. Clinical severity and outcomes of death, cardiac transplant, and continuing left ventricular dysfunction versus echocardiographic normalization were assessed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 279 DCM probands (47% male) with a median (interquartile range) age at diagnosis of 1.6 (0.4-10.4) years were enrolled. Median follow-up was 1.1 (0.2-4.0) years. Gene variants designated as pathogenic/LP were identified in 18 of the 37 genes evaluated, and of all positive variants, TTN (17%), TNNT2 (15%), MYH7 (15%), RBM20 (9%), and LMNA (8%) were most frequently implicated. Only 19% of the overall cohort yielded an identifiable genetic cause, without any difference between ancestries. Children >12 years old had the highest genetic yield at 34% (P<0.05). Symptoms of heart failure occurred in 62% of patients who carried a pathogenic/LP gene variant, at or within 12 months of presentation, but neither heart failure symptoms, nor echocardiographic severity was associated with having a pathogenic/LP variant. The rate of death or cardiac transplant did not differ with the presence or absence of a pathogenic/LP variant and exceeded 60% by 10 years after diagnosis. On competing risks analysis, a trend (P=0.09) toward greater echo normalization, was noted in those without a pathogenic/LP variant by 10 years after diagnosis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A genetic cause was detected in a minority of children and was not associated with the phenotypic severity of DCM at diagnosis. Echocardiographic normalization of left ventricular function over time was noted more frequently in patients who did not have an identified pathogenic/LP variant.

articles.conclusion: A genetic cause was detected in a minority of children and was not associated with the phenotypic severity of DCM at diagnosis. Echocardiographic normalization of left ventricular function over time was noted more frequently in patients who did not have an identified pathogenic/LP variant.

articles.title: Urgent, Emergency, and Salvage Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for Acute Decompensated Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Prospective Cohort Study
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.journal_abbrev: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
articles.ta: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute decompensated severe aortic stenosis may preclude waiting for elective treatment, and evidence for non-elective transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is limited. We assessed 12-month mortality, 30-day safety, and recovery after urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We prospectively enrolled patients undergoing urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI at one centre in 2022-2025. The primary endpoint was 12-month all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included device success, 30-day safety, and functional and echocardiographic recovery.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 53 patients, 36 underwent urgent, 14 emergency, and 3 salvage TAVI. Device success was 52/53 (98.1%). Thirty-day mortality was 1/36, 0/14, and 0/3; 12-month mortality was 2/36, 1/14, and 0/3 (3/53). Kaplan-Meier 12-month survival was 94.3% (95% confidence interval 83.5-98.1%). New atrioventricular block was detected in 2/53 on postoperative day 2; by 30 days, haemofiltration or renal replacement therapy occurred in 1/53 and permanent pacemaker implantation in 0/53. At 12 months, cardiovascular mortality was 2/53, heart-failure readmission 4/53, stroke 1/53, a separate Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 type 2 bleeding event 1/53, and permanent pacemaker implantation 0/53. Paired analyses showed improved New York Heart Association class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12, left ventricular ejection fraction, and transvalvular gradients at 30 days and 12 months (all P<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Selected patients had high device success and low early event rates after non-elective TAVI; paired data showed sustained functional and haemodynamic improvement. These findings support timely Heart Team assessment and consideration of non-elective TAVI, when appropriate, at experienced centres; comparative benefit over alternative strategies warrants prospective study.

articles.conclusion: Selected patients had high device success and low early event rates after non-elective TAVI; paired data showed sustained functional and haemodynamic improvement. These findings support timely Heart Team assessment and consideration of non-elective TAVI, when appropriate, at experienced centres; comparative benefit over alternative strategies warrants prospective study.

articles.title: Therapeutic Targeting of the Macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB Axis Mitigates Pulmonary Hypertension
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.journal_abbrev: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
articles.ta: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

abstract.label: RATIONALE
abstract.text: Immune dysregulation is a pivotal driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, yet therapeutic targeting of inflammation has yielded limited clinical success. Although cytosolic RNA-binding proteins are known to regulate immune responses in PH, the specific role of the nuclear m⁶A reader YTHDC1 remains undefined.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To elucidate the function of macrophage YTHDC1 in orchestrating inflammatory vascular remodeling during PH.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Expression profiles of YTHDC1 and TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) were evaluated in human and rodent PH specimens. The mechanistic and therapeutic roles of this axis were assessed using myeloid-specific knockout mice and pharmacological inhibitors (YL-5092, 5Z-7-oxozeaenol) across hypoxia-, SU5416/hypoxia-, and monocrotaline-induced PH models.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: In patients with idiopathic or connective tissue disease-associated PAH, YTHDC1 and TIGAR expression levels were elevated in pulmonary and circulating macrophages, correlating with disease severity. In murine models, myeloid-specific deletion of Ythdc1 or Tigar conferred profound protection against hypoxia- and SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH. Mechanistically, hypoxia upregulated Ythdc1, which directly bound and stabilized Tigar mRNA. The subsequent accumulation of Tigar protein operated non-enzymatically via a specific domain (residues 152-161) to interact with Tak1, thereby activating the NF-κB cascade, augmenting pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and driving pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell proliferation. Pharmacological inhibition of YTHDC1 (YL-5092) or disruption of the TIGAR-TAK1 interaction (5Z-7-oxozeaenol) effectively attenuated vascular inflammation and mitigated PH progression in diverse rodent models.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB signaling axis acts as a critical determinant of inflammation and vascular remodeling in PH, representing a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for this disease.

articles.conclusion: The macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB signaling axis acts as a critical determinant of inflammation and vascular remodeling in PH, representing a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for this disease.

articles.title: Fabry's Disease, Valvular Disease and Infective Endocarditis: A Rare Intersection

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Infective endocarditis may present with nonspecific systemic symptoms that mimic other conditions, creating diagnostic challenges in high-risk patients.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 44-year-old man with advanced Fabry disease, bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, and a chronic Port-A-Cath presented with fever, chills, and malaise shortly after pegunigalsidase alfa infusion, initially raising concern for an infusion reaction. Persistent methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia prompted further evaluation, revealing right-sided native tricuspid valve infective endocarditis with septal leaflet perforation and severe tricuspid regurgitation. Prosthetic aortic valve involvement remained clinically suspected despite nondiagnostic imaging. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multifocal septic embolic infarctions. He received targeted intravenous antibiotics, catheter removal, multidisciplinary care, and cardiothoracic surgical evaluation, with continued medical management recommended.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case emphasizes maintaining suspicion for infective endocarditis despite a plausible alternative diagnosis and highlights the role of multimodality imaging in guiding management.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Persistent S aureus bacteremia should prompt evaluation for infective endocarditis in high-risk patients even when symptoms initially suggest a plausible alternative diagnosis. Multimodality imaging and multidisciplinary assessment are essential when initial imaging is nondiagnostic or clinical findings suggest embolic complications.

articles.conclusion: This case emphasizes maintaining suspicion for infective endocarditis despite a plausible alternative diagnosis and highlights the role of multimodality imaging in guiding management.

articles.title: Liver Extracellular Volume in Patients With Tricuspid Regurgitation: A Novel Prognostic Marker

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Liver extracellular volume (L-ECV), a novel cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameter of systemic venous congestion, might help to stratify tricuspid regurgitation (TR) patients at higher risk, but its role in this context is unexplored.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to assess the incremental prognostic relevance of L-ECV in a large TR cohort.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data were collected from patients with TR referred to CMR between 2019 and 2024 who had parametric mapping analysis for L-ECV quantification. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization, under medical management.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In 462 patients included (median age: 67 years; 43% female), median left ventricular ejection fraction was 51% (Q1-Q3: 40%-59%), median tricuspid regurgitant fraction was 21% (Q1-Q3: 14%-33%), and median L-ECV was 31% (Q1-Q3: 28%-35%). When dividing the cohort according to median L-ECV value, patients with high L-ECV (≥ median) showed worse baseline status with more clinical and imaging signs of right HF and (after a median follow-up of 2.1 years) poorer survival free from the primary outcome (P < 0.001) compared with patients with low L-ECV. High L-ECV independently predicted the outcome even after multivariable adjustment accounting for TR severity, biventricular ejection fraction, and pulmonary pressure (adjusted HR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.03-3.18; P = 0.030). Finally, L-ECV showed incremental prognostic value compared with TRI-SCORE when assessed in a nested Cox model.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In our large real-world TR cohort, L-ECV appeared as a novel, powerful CMR marker of right HF with an independent and incremental prognostic value to stratify patients with TR at higher risk of events.

articles.conclusion: In our large real-world TR cohort, L-ECV appeared as a novel, powerful CMR marker of right HF with an independent and incremental prognostic value to stratify patients with TR at higher risk of events.

articles.title: Salvage Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve With Aspiration Thrombectomy in a Young Adult With Repaired CHD

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Prosthetic mitral valve degeneration in adults with repaired congenital heart disease (CHD) can produce rapid hemodynamic collapse and is challenging when surgery and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) are unavailable.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 20-year-old woman with congenital mitral stenosis and multiple ventricular septal defects initially palliated as a single ventricle, then converted to biventricular circulation, with prior mechanical and bioprosthetic mitral valve replacements (the latter for menorrhagia, outside our care), presented in cardiogenic shock with prosthetic mitral stenosis and acute left atrial thrombus. Hypoplastic peripheral vessels precluded MCS. Salvage valve-in-valve was performed with bilateral cerebral protection, FlowTriever thrombectomy (Inari Medical), and a 26-mm SAPIEN 3 valve (Edwards Lifesciences).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve can be lifesaving in adults with repaired CHD when intracardiac thrombus is present, and MCS is unavailable.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: In highly selected, life-threatening presentations without alternatives, salvage transcatheter mitral intervention may be considered despite intracardiac thrombus. Peripheral vascular anatomy must be evaluated preprocedurally in complex CHD.

articles.title: Donor-Recipient Sex Mismatch is Associated with Severe Primary Graft Dysfunction after Heart Transplantation
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The association between sex and primary graft dysfunction after heart transplantation (HT) remains unclear. We evaluated whether recipient sex and donor-recipient sex matching are associated with severe primary graft dysfunction (PGD) in a contemporary, multicenter cohort.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed data from the International PGD Consortium comprised of adult HTs from 2010 to 2024 across 14 centers. Associations between sex-related variables and severe PGD were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, and adjusted for ischemic time, pre-transplant durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD), dialysis, congenital heart disease, and predicted heart mass (PHM) ratio.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 3,994 recipients, 1,030 (25.8%) were female. Female recipients were younger (54 vs. 57 years) with fewer comorbidities, and less frequently bridged on a durable LVAD (19.8% vs. 29.1%). Although female recipients had a lower incidence of PGD than male recipients (7.1% vs. 9.4%), recipient sex was not independently associated with PGD after multivariable adjustment. Female donor to male recipient sex mismatching had the highest PGD incidence of 11.5% and was associated with a 43% increase in the odds of severe PGD (p=0.030). While sex-mismatch was associated with an increased incidence of PGD, size mismatch by PHM ratio was not an independent predictor.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this large international registry, donor-recipient sex mismatch, specifically among male recipients of female donor hearts, was independently associated with severe PGD, even when appropriately size matched. These findings inform risk stratification for development of severe PGD after HT.

articles.conclusion: In this large international registry, donor-recipient sex mismatch, specifically among male recipients of female donor hearts, was independently associated with severe PGD, even when appropriately size matched. These findings inform risk stratification for development of severe PGD after HT.

articles.title: Resource Utilization and Forecasting in Heart Failure Patients with Durable Left Ventricular Assist Devices
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstract.text: Heart failure patients treated with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) require significant resource utilization. Patient volume and contact points based on implant volume remain poorly quantified. We retrospectively reviewed 268 patients implanted with a durable LVAD at a single, experienced center from 2011 through 2022 and recorded survival, telephone encounters, office visits, and all-cause hospitalizations. Telephone encounters peaked at 10.4 per patient-month and declined to approximately 5 after 24 months; 66% were anticoagulation-related. Office visits peaked at 3.0 per patient-month and declined to approximately 0.7 after 18 months. Hospitalizations decreased from 2.7 per patient-year in year 1 to approximately 1 by year 5. Five-year survival with HeartMate 3 (HM3) was 61.4%. Applying HM3 survival to constant annual implant volumes yielded estimated 5-year censuses of 39, 96, and 193 surviving patients for 10, 25, and 50 annual implants, respectively. These findings may inform LVAD program capacity and staffing.

articles.title: Association Between Elevated Donor-Derived Cell-Free DNA and Donor-Specific Antibodies in Heart Transplantation: Antibody-Mediated Rejection and Long-Term Outcomes
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) and donor-specific antibodies (DSA) are both used for non-invasive surveillance after heart transplantation (HT). Whether DSA provides incremental value beyond dd-cfDNA for detecting antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) and predicting outcomes is uncertain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this single-center retrospective study of adult HT recipients with paired dd-cfDNA and DSA results (September 2019 to December 2024), biopsies within 30 days of sampling were paired for analysis. Significant rejection was defined as acute cellular rejection (ACR) grade ≥2R and/or AMR (pAMR ≥1). Associations were modeled among biopsy-paired samples using patient-clustered generalized estimating equations, and mortality using time-dependent Cox and Bayesian joint models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We analyzed 2,856 dd-cfDNA/DSA pairs from 287 recipients, of which 763 were biopsy-paired. Elevated dd-cfDNA was more frequent in DSA-positive samples (19.3% vs 10.5%; p=0.006). Among biopsied samples, AMR was associated with DSA (OR 5.93, 95% CI 1.82-19.26) and elevated dd-cfDNA (OR 6.21, 95% CI 2.07-18.60). Relative to negative concordance, the risk of significant rejection was similar with isolated DSA-positivity (OR 3.83) and isolated dd-cfDNA-positivity (OR 3.80) and was highest with double-positivity (OR 15.70, 95% CI 4.71-52.30). Adding DSA with MFI ≥4000 to dd-cfDNA increased the AUC for AMR from 0.73 to 0.84 (p=0.03). Among 15 deaths, dd-cfDNA, but not DSA, was associated with mortality (HR 2.12, 95% CrI 1.24-3.39).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: dd-cfDNA and DSA carried similar, additive information for rejection, with double-positivity identifying the highest-risk phenotype. In exploratory analyses, DSA at MFI ≥4000 added to dd-cfDNA for AMR, and dd-cfDNA was the only marker associated with mortality.

articles.conclusion: dd-cfDNA and DSA carried similar, additive information for rejection, with double-positivity identifying the highest-risk phenotype. In exploratory analyses, DSA at MFI ≥4000 added to dd-cfDNA for AMR, and dd-cfDNA was the only marker associated with mortality.

articles.title: AAOLCA in a Child Presenting With Fever and Cardiac Arrest: Diagnostic Overlap With Acute Myocarditis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Anomalous aortic origin of the left coronary artery (AAOLCA) is a rare congenital coronary anomaly causing myocardial ischemia and sudden cardiac death. Despite differing in pathophysiology from acute myocarditis, AAOLCA can present with a clinically indistinguishable acute picture.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: We report an 11-year-old child with no prior cardiac history presenting with fever (40 °C), syncope, cardiac arrest, and cardiogenic shock. Elevated troponin and reduced ejection fraction initially suggested acute myocarditis, which could not be excluded. Atypical features-absent arrhythmia, rapid biomarker normalization, and fluctuating ventricular function-prompted further evaluation. Echocardiography and coronary angiography identified AAOLCA with a hemodynamically significant intramural segment; dynamic ischemia was confirmed during angiography. Surgical unroofing resulted in clinical recovery.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: AAOLCA should be considered when pediatric myocarditis presents atypically. Echocardiography is essential. When concurrent myocarditis cannot be excluded, surgical timing should be individualized; here, a period of stabilization preceded definitive repair.

articles.conclusion: AAOLCA should be considered when pediatric myocarditis presents atypically. Echocardiography is essential. When concurrent myocarditis cannot be excluded, surgical timing should be individualized; here, a period of stabilization preceded definitive repair.

articles.title: Colchicine improves the diastolic performance in HFpEF myocardium
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.journal_abbrev: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.ta: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstract.text: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) arises from increased ventricular stiffening and impaired relaxation with cardiac microtubules recently identified as a source of both. This has motivated the development of cardiac-specific microtubule modifying treatments for heart failure as more common microtubule-depolymerizing agents such as colchicine have limited clinical tolerance from systemic effects. Nevertheless, low-dose colchicine is a commonly prescribed anti-inflammatory compound and has recently shown positive indication for the treatment of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and HFpEF. This raises the question whether colchicine directly improves myocardial performance. Herein we leverage recent advancements in living myocardial slices via a preparation that recapitulates physiological loading and the complexity of diastole to determine if colchicine can directly improve diastolic performance in a rat model of cardiometabolic diastolic heart disease. We found that working slices from obese rats maintained the hallmark mechanical features of HFpEF: namely, preserved force generation and work output, diastolic dysfunction by reduced E/A ratio and an inability to maintain work output at elevated contractile frequencies. Treatment with colchicine had insignificant effects on isometric twitch force but significantly enhanced ejection and filling efficiencies by restoring early filling performance. These data are therefore consistent with colchicine improving the mechanical properties of the myocardium through microtubule destabilization thereby enhancing the efficiency of myocardial movement without significantly altering force generation.

articles.title: Targeting PLN-R14del cardiomyopathy in mice using DWORF gene therapy suggests the necessity of high expression levels
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.journal_abbrev: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.ta: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstract.text: There is currently no successful treatment for patients with cardiomyopathy caused by the p.Arg14del mutation in the phospholamban (PLN) gene, other than heart transplantation. Interestingly, transgenic overexpression of the small peptide Dwarf open reading frame (DWORF) could delay disease development and extend life span in a PLN-R14del cardiomyopathy mouse model. Here, we evaluated the potential of DWORF gene therapy using adeno-associated virus cardiotropic serotype 9 (AAV9) in a PLN-R14del mouse model. At postnatal day 7, AAV9-cTnT-DWORF (AAV-DWORF) or control AAV9-cTnT-luciferase (AAV-luciferase) was delivered to homozygous PLN-R14del (R14Δ/Δ) mice. The AAV-DWORF construct targeted the majority of cardiomyocytes in the heart, as shown by in situ RNA labeling. Moreover, it significantly increased DWORF protein expression by fivefold, but did not reach the same high 25-fold increased expression level as observed in a DWORF transgenic mice. Previous study showed that high transgenic DWORF expression was able to delay PLN-R14del cardiac impairment and preserved cardiac ejection fraction (EF) in 6-week-old mice. However, the current study reveals that AAV-DWORF did not delay the decline in EF of R14Δ/Δ mice. This was corroborated by the observation that the R14Δ/Δ-induced increase of heart failure markers and cardiac fibrosis were not inhibited by AAV-DWORF. In conclusion, whereas high transgenic DWORF overexpression can delay cardiac dysfunction in a PLN-R14del mouse model, a fivefold lower AAV-mediated overexpression was not sufficient to delay disease progression. This suggests that only high supraphysiological DWORF levels are able to delay disease development, requiring further optimization of AAV-DWORF therapy.

articles.title: Procedural Volume and Outcomes After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty for Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is an established treatment for inoperable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension; however, volume-outcome relationships remain unclear.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study examined the relationship between hospital and operator volume and BPA-related complications using a nationwide registry.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The authors analyzed 5,403 BPA sessions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension in the Japanese Structural Heart Diseases registry between 2021 and 2024. Procedural volume was defined as BPA sessions performed during the preceding 3 years. The primary outcome was a composite of BPA-related complications. Mixed-effects logistic regression models accounted for hospital and operator clustering.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: BPA-related complications occurred in 751 sessions (13.9%). Severe complications were uncommon, with 3 periprocedural deaths, 6 requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, and 7 requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. The main categorical analysis revealed that hospital BPA volume ≥150 sessions/3 years was associated with higher odds of BPA-related complications (adjusted OR: 1.60; 95% CI: 1.08-2.36; P = 0.019), whereas operator volume was not independently associated. When hospital and operator volumes were modeled separately as continuous variables, each was associated with complications. However, neither remained independently associated after mutual adjustment. In an analysis restricted to 135 complications considered less susceptible to differences in ascertainment, no statistically significant association was detected for either volume measure, although the smaller number of events limited statistical precision.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: BPA-related complications demonstrated a complex relationship with procedural volume, while severe complications remained uncommon. The attenuation of hospital- and operator-level associations after mutual adjustment suggests that procedural volume alone may not adequately characterize BPA safety. Further studies incorporating lesion- and procedural-level characteristics and standardized complication ascertainment are warranted.

articles.conclusion: BPA-related complications demonstrated a complex relationship with procedural volume, while severe complications remained uncommon. The attenuation of hospital- and operator-level associations after mutual adjustment suggests that procedural volume alone may not adequately characterize BPA safety. Further studies incorporating lesion- and procedural-level characteristics and standardized complication ascertainment are warranted.

articles.title: Severe dynamic left-ventricular outflow-tract obstruction unmasked by transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Relieving the fixed afterload of severe aortic stenosis can unmask a previously concealed dynamic outflow-tract obstruction.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 69-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.65 cm2; 109/64 mmHg), mild concentric hypertrophy (septum 15 mm), and no baseline systolic anterior motion (SAM) underwent transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). The invasive peak-to-peak gradient fell from 64 to 7 mmHg, but echocardiography immediately afterwards showed new SAM and severe dynamic left-ventricular-outflow-tract (LVOT) obstruction (170/67 mmHg) with hypotension. Treatment was load-directed (volume expansion, avoidance of vasodilators and inotropes, beta-blockade), with a cardiac myosin inhibitor as an adjunct. Over 4 months the resting LVOT gradient fell to 22/13 mmHg and the provoked peak to 29 mmHg, with SAM no longer seen and preserved ejection fraction.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Recognizing this load-dependent obstruction during the procedure and restoring loading, rather than escalating inotropes, is the key lesson.

articles.title: Skeletal muscle oxidative capacity and tissue composition in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

abstract.text: Increasing evidence suggests that exercise intolerance in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is related to peripheral abnormalities; however, the roles of muscle oxidative capacity and muscle steatosis remain incompletely understood. To address this knowledge gap, 38 HFpEF patients [mean age 69.8 ± 6.1 yr, body mass index (BMI) 37.6 ± 6.9 kg/m2] and 17 healthy older adults (HOAs; mean age 67.6 ± 5.4 yr, BMI 27.3 ± 4.8 kg/m2) performed a graded exercise test on a cycle ergometer to assess exercise tolerance (peak watts) and whole body aerobic capacity [peak O2 uptake (V̇o2peak)]. In vivo quadriceps oxidative capacity [phosphocreatine recovery time constant (τPCr)] and thigh tissue composition [i.e., lean thigh mass (LTM); intermuscular fat % (IMF%)] were measured separately via 31P-magnetic resonance spectroscopy (31P-MRS) and T2-weighted MRI, respectively. LTM was similar between HFpEF patients and HOAs (P = 0.854), but IMF% was significantly greater in HFpEF (P ≤ 0.001). Peak watts and V̇o2peak normalized to LTM were lower and quadriceps τPCr was slower in HFpEF patients compared to HOAs (all P < 0.03). Although IMF% was associated with peak watts normalized to LTM (R2 = 0.148) and whole body V̇o2peak normalized to body mass (R2 = 0.347), it was not associated with V̇o2peak normalized to LTM (R2 < 0.001) or τPCr (R2 = 0.020). In contrast, V̇o2peak normalized to LTM and quadriceps τPCr were both associated with peak watts (R2 = 0.509 and 0.252, respectively) and with each other (R2 = 0.298). Taken together, these data suggest that exercise intolerance in HFpEF is associated with increased muscle steatosis and impaired whole body and quadriceps muscle oxidative capacity. However, the lack of association between IMF% and measures of oxidative capacity suggest that they affect exercise tolerance via different physiological mechanisms.NEW & NOTEWORTHY We compared peripheral mechanisms of exercise intolerance in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) patients and healthy older adults. HFpEF patients exhibited significantly greater intermuscular steatosis and impaired whole body and quadriceps oxidative capacity [i.e., peak O2 uptake (V̇o2peak) and phosphocreatine recovery time constant (τPCr), respectively], all of which were associated with impaired exercise tolerance. However, increased intermuscular steatosis was not associated with impaired V̇o2peak and τPCr, suggesting that steatosis and impaired oxidative capacity affect exercise tolerance through different physiological mechanisms.

articles.title: The clinical chameleon: eosinophilic myocarditis presenting as acute coronary syndrome-a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Eosinophilic myocarditis is a rare inflammatory cardiomyopathy that may clinically mimic acute coronary syndrome and should be considered in patients with non-obstructive coronary arteries, often resulting in diagnostic delay.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 27-year-old man presented with recurrent chest pain and was initially misdiagnosed with a panic attack. On admission, laboratory evaluation revealed marked peripheral eosinophilia (1800/mm3), mildly elevated troponin, and increased serum IgE levels. Echocardiography demonstrated reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and a large apical intracavitary thrombus. Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed myocardial oedema and circumferential subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement consistent with eosinophilic myocarditis. Extensive aetiological workup was negative. Although endomyocardial biopsy showed non-specific findings, the diagnosis was established through multimodal integration of clinical, imaging, and laboratory data. High-dose corticosteroid therapy and anticoagulation resulted in rapid clinical improvement, recovery of ventricular function, and near-complete thrombus resolution.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Eosinophilic myocarditis should be considered in young patients presenting with chest pain and non-obstructive coronary arteries. Multimodality imaging-particularly cardiac magnetic resonance-plays a key role in diagnosis, while early corticosteroid therapy may lead to rapid clinical and functional recovery.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of clinical suspicion for EM in young patients presenting with chest pain and peripheral eosinophilia. A multimodal diagnostic approach integrating cMRI findings, laboratory data, and exclusion of alternative aetiologies is essential when biopsy results are inconclusive. Early immunosuppressive therapy is key to reversing myocardial damage and preventing progression to end-stage heart failure.

articles.conclusion: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of clinical suspicion for EM in young patients presenting with chest pain and peripheral eosinophilia. A multimodal diagnostic approach integrating cMRI findings, laboratory data, and exclusion of alternative aetiologies is essential when biopsy results are inconclusive. Early immunosuppressive therapy is key to reversing myocardial damage and preventing progression to end-stage heart failure.

articles.title: Norepinephrine Equivalent Dose for Mortality Risk Stratification in VA-ECMO Cardiogenic Shock

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) complicated by vasoplegia requiring venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) often need escalating vasopressor support and face high mortality. Norepinephrine equivalent dose (NEE) quantifies vasopressor burden, yet its prognostic value in VA-ECMO remains undefined.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We aimed to characterize the dose-response relationship between NEE and 30-day mortality, identify a clinically relevant NEE threshold, and determine factors associated with high vasopressor burden.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This bicentric retrospective study included 572 consecutive patients with CS requiring VA-ECMO. We collected vasopressor regimens, NEE trajectories, and hemodynamic parameters at predefined intervals. Restricted cubic splines assessed dose-response linearity. Maximally selected rank statistics with bootstrap validation identified optimal thresholds. Cox models estimated mortality risk. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with high vasopressor burden.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median NEE at ECMO initiation was 0.30 (IQR: 0.09-0.72) μg·kg-1·min-1; 86.2% received norepinephrine. NEE showed a linear dose-response with mortality (HR: 1.06 per 0.1 μg·kg-1·min-1 increment; 95% CI: 1.04-1.08; P < 0.001). A threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 identified high vasopressor burden with elevated 30-day mortality (61.8% vs 42.6%; P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 1.42; 95% CI: 1.11-1.81; P = 0.005). Factors associated with high vasopressor burden included mechanical ventilation (OR: 2.96; 95% CI: 1.08-8.07), prior epinephrine use (OR: 1.87; 95% CI: 1.12-3.14), renal replacement therapy before VA-ECMO (OR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.02-3.03), baseline lactate (OR: 1.05 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 1.01-1.09), and lower Survival After Veno-Arterial ECMO score (OR: 0.96 per point; 95% CI: 0.92-1.00). Left ventricular unloading was inversely associated (OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.34-0.87).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In VA-ECMO-supported CS with vasoplegia, vasopressor burden shows a linear relationship with mortality. A NEE threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 may identify patients with elevated mortality risk.

articles.conclusion: In VA-ECMO-supported CS with vasoplegia, vasopressor burden shows a linear relationship with mortality. A NEE threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 may identify patients with elevated mortality risk.

articles.title: Multi-modal AI: Integrating electrocardiography with molecular biomarkers for noninvasive detection of cardiac allograft rejection

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Noninvasive rejection biomarkers (AlloMap, AlloSure) demonstrate high negative predictive value but positive predictive values of only 10-30%, driving avoidable endomyocardial biopsies. We developed a multi-modal AI model integrating electrocardiography with molecular biomarkers in 389 heart transplant recipients (5338 ECG-biopsy pairs), performing the first head-to-head comparison of AI-ECG, AlloMap, AlloSure, and their integration against biopsy-proven rejection. Individual modalities showed modest discrimination (AI-ECG AUC 0.65; AlloSure 0.67; AlloMap 0.56), while combining biomarkers alone did not improve performance (AUC 0.65). In the multi-modal test subset of ECGs (n=38, 2 rejection events), the integrated model achieved AUC 0.81 with 100% specificity (0/36 false positives) and 97% negative predictive value, eliminating all 19 false-positive combined-biomarker referrals. These hypothesis-generating results support prospective multi-center validation to determine whether requiring concordance across electrical and biomarker signals reduces unnecessary biopsies while preserving high negative predictive value.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Noninvasive rejection biomarkers (AlloMap gene-expression profiling (GEP); AlloSure donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA)) deliver high negative predictive value but positive predictive values of only 10-30%, driving avoidable endomyocardial biopsies. Each biomarker interrogates a single biological compartment. Whether integrating AI-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) with these molecular assays improves specificity has not been tested.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively assembled 5338 unique ECG-endomyocardial-biopsy pairs from 389 adult heart transplant recipients at a single center (2018-2024). A ResNet-18 convolutional neural network was trained on 8-lead ECG waveforms with clinical covariates. In the 340-patient subset with same encounter AlloMap and AlloSure testing (405 ECG-biomarker-biopsy triplets), an integrated model fused the ECG embedding with biomarker values via late concatenation. We performed the first head-to-head, same-cohort comparison of AI-ECG, AlloMap, AlloSure, and their integration against biopsy-proven rejection (ISHLT ≥2R ACR or pAMR ≥2). Discrimination was evaluated with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Individual modalities showed modest discrimination (AI-ECG AUC 0.65, 95% CI 0.58-0.72; AlloSure 0.67, 0.56-0.78; AlloMap 0.56, 0.46-0.67); combining biomarkers alone did not improve performance (AUC 0.65). In the multi-modal test subset (n=38 ECG-biopsy pairs, 2 rejection events), the integrated model achieved AUC 0.81 (0.50-1.00), 100% specificity (36/36; Clopper-Pearson 90-100%), and 97% NPV. At the same NPV threshold, all 19 false-positive combined-biomarker referrals in this subset would have been avoided, though this estimate reflects a single operating point in a small sample. AUC gains over single modalities did not reach statistical significance (DeLong p=0.31-0.34) given the limited event count.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A multi-modal AI model that requires concordance across electrical, immune-transcriptional, and donor-DNA signals showed numerically higher specificity for cardiac allograft rejection than any single modality, although the corresponding AUC differences did not reach statistical significance. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that cross-compartment concordance may help discriminate true rejection from biomarker noise, but the small multi-modal test set precludes definitive conclusions; a pre-specified prospective multi-center trial powered for ≥50 rejection events is the necessary next step to test this hypothesis.

articles.conclusion: A multi-modal AI model that requires concordance across electrical, immune-transcriptional, and donor-DNA signals showed numerically higher specificity for cardiac allograft rejection than any single modality, although the corresponding AUC differences did not reach statistical significance. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that cross-compartment concordance may help discriminate true rejection from biomarker noise, but the small multi-modal test set precludes definitive conclusions; a pre-specified prospective multi-center trial powered for ≥50 rejection events is the necessary next step to test this hypothesis.

articles.title: Utilization of Preventive Single-Inflow Cannula Left Atrial Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Cardiogenic Shock
articles.journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Left ventricular/left ventricle (LV) overload remains a major limitation of veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) in patients with cardiogenic shock. Left atrial veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (LAVA-ECMO) has been proposed to facilitate LV unloading; however, data regarding its optimal timing and clinical role remain limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated the efficacy and safety of a preventive single-inflow cannula LAVA-ECMO strategy, defined as an a priori LV unloading approach implemented at extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) initiation, either through primary LAVA-ECMO implantation or planned early conversion from VA-ECMO within 60 minutes. Between January 2020 and July 2025, eligible patients supported with VA-ECMO or LAVA-ECMO were screened. After predefined exclusions, 42 patients managed with preventive LAVA-ECMO were compared with 64 contemporaneous patients receiving conventional VA-ECMO.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-day all-cause mortality was lower in the LAVA-ECMO group than in the VA-ECMO group (47.6% vs 76.6%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.31-0.95). Failure to wean from ECMO tended to occur less frequently with LAVA-ECMO (31.0% vs 56.3%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.18-1.01). Signs of LV overload during ECMO support were significantly reduced in the LAVA-ECMO group (47.6% vs 82.8%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.19, 95% CI, 0.08-0.49). Overall complication rates were comparable between groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this retrospective cohort, preventive LAVA-ECMO was associated with lower short-term mortality and a reduced incidence of LV overload without an apparent increase in complications. Preventive LAVA-ECMO may represent a feasible mechanical circulatory support strategy in carefully selected patients with cardiogenic shock.

articles.conclusion: In this retrospective cohort, preventive LAVA-ECMO was associated with lower short-term mortality and a reduced incidence of LV overload without an apparent increase in complications. Preventive LAVA-ECMO may represent a feasible mechanical circulatory support strategy in carefully selected patients with cardiogenic shock.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Large-Bore Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis for Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A PEERLESS Randomized Controlled Trial Post Hoc Analysis
articles.journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (LBMT) compared with catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) for the treatment of intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A combined decision tree and Markov model was developed to estimate lifetime health care costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALY), and net monetary benefit from the perspective of the United States health care system. Event probabilities during PE management were derived from the PEERLESS randomized controlled trial. Resource utilization, costs, and long-term event probabilities were established from published literature. Scenario analyses and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed to characterize uncertainty.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the base case analysis, LBMT was cost-saving to CDT (ie, lower costs and higher QALY), with a net monetary benefit of $5850 for the willingness-to-pay threshold of $120,000/QALY for LBMT when compared to CDT. In the PE management phase, LBMT yielded a net $4755 cost-saving and 0.009 QALY gained per patient vs CDT, driven in large part by reduced intensive care unit utilization (-$6454), shorter hospital stay (-$2217), avoided thrombolytic costs (-$4068), and fewer 30-day readmissions (-$1134). The long-term care phase yielded a total of $32,012 additional costs per patient over the lifetime with no incremental difference in costs or QALY between groups. These additional costs were driven by venous thromboembolism-related death ($12,377), chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension diagnosis and treatment ($8080), postacute anticoagulation management ($4512), and recurrent venous thromboembolism ($3289). LBMT remained cost-saving across scenarios evaluating CDT cost assumptions and device-specific chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension rates. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings across multiple parameter ranges.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Intervention with LBMT in intermediate-risk PE patients in the United States is economically attractive when compared with CDT, resulting in reduced costs and marginally improved patient benefit.

articles.conclusion: Intervention with LBMT in intermediate-risk PE patients in the United States is economically attractive when compared with CDT, resulting in reduced costs and marginally improved patient benefit.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Concurrent Impella-Assisted High-Risk PCI and TAVR in Patients With Complex Coronary Artery Disease and Severe Aortic Stenosis
articles.journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Percutaneous management of high risk, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) needing mechanical support for complex coronary artery disease in patients needing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis remains incompletely defined. We report on the feasibility and safety of a single-session strategy using Impella-assisted complex high-risk PCI (IA-CHIP) followed by transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing simultaneous IA-CHIP and TAVR at 3 tertiary centers between January 2015 and March 2026. All patients received mechanical circulatory support with percutaneous microaxial flow pump Impella CP (Abiomed) during PCI, followed by transfemoral TAVR in the same session. Baseline demographics, procedural characteristics, and clinical outcomes were collected. The primary endpoint was in-hospital complications, including death, stroke, major bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 2, 3, or 5), acute kidney injury, permanent pacemaker implantation, and vascular complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 12 patients were included (median age, 79.5 years [IQR, 77.0-81.2]; 91.7% male; median Charlson Comorbidity Index of 7 [IQR, 5.8-9]). Coronary lesions mainly involved left main disease in 66% of cases. Advanced calcium modification was required in 50% of cases. The median aortic valve area was 0.86 cm2, and median mean gradient was 38 mm Hg. Procedural success for IA-CHIP and TAVR was 100%. There were no in-hospital deaths, strokes, or major vascular complications. Conduction disturbances requiring permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 25%. An acute kidney injury occurred in 16.7% of cases, with no requirement for dialysis. The majority of patients (91.7%) were discharged home.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A single-session strategy of IA-CHIP followed by TAVR is feasible and safe in selected patients with complex coronary artery disease and severe aortic stenosis.

articles.conclusion: A single-session strategy of IA-CHIP followed by TAVR is feasible and safe in selected patients with complex coronary artery disease and severe aortic stenosis.

articles.title: Optimal Sheath for Single-Access Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Impella CP Hemodynamic Support
articles.journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Single-access percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the Impella CP (Abiomed) has increased in prevalence. Despite this, the optimal PCI sheath remains unknown. We characterized the optimal 7F PCI sheath using the single-access technique.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The outer diameter measurement of the sheaths was performed using a Keyence 2-axis laser micrometer (Keyence). The force needed to insert the sheath and the torqueability of the guide catheter were assessed using the Mark-10 M5i Advanced Digital Force/Torque Indicator (Mark-10 Corporation) on a simulated single-access setting in a simulated skin pad. The sample size was determined to be 5 sheaths for each test.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The BRITE TIP 11 cm (Cordis), BRITE TIP 35 cm (Cordis), and Destination sheath (Terumo) had the largest outer diameters; the Prelude IDeal (Merit Medical) and Terumo Glidesheath (Terumo) had the smallest outer diameters. The Glidesheath was easiest for insertion/removal, followed by the Prelude IDeal and Impella Low Profile (LP) Companion sheath (Abiomed). The Impella LP Companion, Prelude Roadster (Merit Medical), and Destination sheaths allowed for the best torqueability and lowest force to remove the guide catheter. The longer Impella LP Companion sheath did not impact torqueability, but the removal force increased by 50% compared with the shorter Impella LP Companion sheath.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The Impella LP Companion sheath demonstrated the best torqueability and least effort in advancing the guide catheters, while the Prelude Roadster and Destination also performed well on these metrics. The Prelude IDeal and Glidesheath were good options for single-access because of their smaller outer diameters and hydrophilic coating and were easiest for insertion/removal through the 14F LP sheath.

articles.conclusion: The Impella LP Companion sheath demonstrated the best torqueability and least effort in advancing the guide catheters, while the Prelude Roadster and Destination also performed well on these metrics. The Prelude IDeal and Glidesheath were good options for single-access because of their smaller outer diameters and hydrophilic coating and were easiest for insertion/removal through the 14F LP sheath.
